chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from al-Mu'alla from al-Washsha' said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who emancipates his slave while he is in good condition, then later needs money; is it permissible for him to sell the slave? He said, 'Yes, if he needs to do so.'

key_terms.يُدَبِّرُ: Emancipates (specifically tadbir, a form of partial emancipation)

ai.seo_question: Can a master sell a slave after emancipating them if he needs money?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the concept of *tadbir* is clarified not as immediate emancipation, but as a conditional status where the slave remains bound until the master's death, yet retains a marketable value. The Imam permits the master to sell the *mudabbir* slave in times of financial necessity, highlighting the practical flexibility of this legal institution within Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the balance between the spiritual merit of eventual emancipation and the economic realities of the master.
